children: CBL & Associates Properties, Inc.

’s CBL investors have been gaining from the stock over the past year. Shares of the Chattanooga, TN-based self-managed, integrated real estate investment trust (REIT) surged 77.1% in the past year compared with the industry’s 10.7% gain. It has also outperformed the sector and the S&P 500’s gains of 8% and 17.5%, respectively, in the same time frame.
Two major developments of CBL in recent months include the sale of York Town Center in York, PA, and the announcement of its promising second-quarter 2026 results (both in August).

In the second quarter, CBL reported robust revenues and earnings, supported by higher rental income, improved occupancy and gains from real estate activity. Same-center net operating income (NOI) increased as higher occupancy, contractual rent escalations and percentage rents supported rental revenue, while funds from operations (FFO), as adjusted, per share also improved.

Management highlighted robust leasing demand, positive lease spreads and improving tenant sales across the portfolio. CBL continued to diversify its tenant mix with retail, dining, entertainment and experiential uses, while advancing portfolio repositioning through property and land sales. The company also completed refinancing activity that extended maturities, unlocked cash flow and increased financial flexibility.
CBL’s One-Year Price Comparison
Over the past year, the stock’s performance has remained strong, outperforming its peers like
Kimco Realty Corporation
KIM and
Federal Realty Investment Trust
FRT. Kimco Realty and Federal Realty Investment’s shares have gained 2.9% and 10.6%, respectively, in the same time frame.

Despite broader risks from shifts in consumer spending and changing financing conditions, the favorable share price movement suggests CBL is well-positioned to sustain its positive momentum at present.

CBL is a self-managed, fully integrated REIT that owns and operates regional shopping malls, lifestyle centers, outlet centers and open-air centers. Its properties primarily generate revenues from tenant leases, including rental income and tenant reimbursements.
CBL's Operating and Portfolio Momentum

CBL continues to benefit from healthy leasing demand across its portfolio. New and renewal activity remained robust, lease spreads were positive and portfolio occupancy improved from the prior year. These trends are supporting higher rental revenues and same-center NOI, while the improvement in FFO, as adjusted, provides additional evidence that stronger property-level fundamentals are translating into operating performance.

CBL is actively broadening the uses available at its properties beyond traditional retail. New dining, entertainment and experiential concepts, together with anchor and junior-anchor upgrades, are intended to create additional traffic sources and strengthen the appeal of its centers. Management’s continued focus on merchandising vacant and former anchor space should also help improve the quality of the tenant mix and support sales productivity across the portfolio.

CBL is reshaping its asset base by disposing of selected non-core and open-air properties while directing capital toward dominant malls in middle markets. The company is also monetizing excess land and underused parcels for non-retail development. This strategy will likely improve portfolio quality, reduce exposure to weaker assets and redeploy capital toward properties with stronger cash-flow and return characteristics.
CBL's Balance Sheet and Shareholder Returns

Recent refinancing activity has extended CBL’s maturity profile, reduced near-term financing risk and released cash flow that had previously been restricted. At the same time, management continues to reduce debt and resolve lower-yielding property obligations. These actions strengthen the balance sheet and improve the durability of cash generation without relying on operating improvements alone.

CBL has increased its regular dividend as stronger cash generation and refinancing benefits have improved its capacity for shareholder distributions. Looking ahead, the scheduled expiration of Section 382 limitations could also provide greater flexibility to monetize assets and potentially return capital in a more tax-efficient manner, adding another potential shareholder-return driver.
Challenges Ahead of CBL

CBL faces two key challenges. First, its results remain exposed to shifts in consumer spending and tenant health, as weaker retail demand, bankruptcies or store closures could pressure occupancy, leasing economics and property cash flows. Second, the company remains sensitive to financing conditions because its business carries substantial property-level debt. Tighter credit markets or higher borrowing costs could complicate refinancing, constrain cash available for distributions and limit flexibility for portfolio investment.
CBL Stock’s Valuation
CBL's trailing 12-month EV/Sales of 2.5X is lower than the industry’s average of 15X but is higher than its five-year median of 1.3X.
Kimco Realty and Federal Realty Investment’s trailing 12-month EV/Sales currently stand at 10.6X and 10.8X, respectively, in the same time frame.
Our Final Take on CBL

CBL’s strong share-price performance has been supported by improving property fundamentals. Healthy leasing demand, higher occupancy and positive lease spreads have supported rental growth and same-center NOI, while continued tenant-mix diversification is strengthening the operating backdrop across the portfolio.

Portfolio repositioning and balance-sheet progress are also supporting the stock. CBL is reallocating capital toward stronger assets while monetizing non-core properties and underused land. At the same time, refinancing activity has improved its maturity profile, reduced financing pressure and enhanced financial flexibility.

However, sustaining the momentum will require continued execution. CBL remains exposed to changes in consumer spending and tenant health, while unfavorable financing conditions could increase borrowing costs and limit flexibility for investment and shareholder distributions.

From a valuation standpoint, CBL trades at a discount to the broader industry but above its own historical norm. For investors, this suggests that the stock may still appear relatively inexpensive compared with industry peers, but its premium to its historical valuation indicates that expectations have strengthened following the improvement in operating performance and financial flexibility.

For existing shareholders, stronger property fundamentals, portfolio optimization and balance-sheet improvements provide support for staying invested. Prospective investors may also find the stock worth considering, although the valuation relative to its own history suggests that further upside will increasingly depend on CBL sustaining leasing momentum, improving portfolio quality and translating its financial flexibility into durable cash-flow growth.
